# Reference pictures for Seedance — a diffusr guide

How to make and pass references for make_video on the Seedance models. The same rules keep a person, a product and a room the same from shot to shot and from clip to clip.

## How Seedance reads references

- Every picture in image_urls is a REFERENCE, never a locked first frame: the model takes from it what the prompt says. To open on a picture, say so — "Image 1 is the exact first frame of this clip; continue directly from it." The video will look like it, not match it pixel for pixel.
- Pictures are numbered in image_urls order — Image 1, Image 2… — and voice clips in audio_urls order — Audio 1, Audio 2… (@Image1 works too).
- Bind every reference at the top of the prompt, one line each: what it is and what to take from it.

```
Image 1 is Mia, the speaker: keep her face, hair and outfit exactly as in Image 1.
Image 2 is the object "Glow Serum"; keep it exactly as shown.
Image 3 is the setting "the kitchen"; stage the scene in it.
Audio 1 is Mia's voice: keep the same voice, tone and pace.
```

- The binding line is the only label. Never write a name on a picture ("MIA" on a sheet): the model can duplicate or swap people.
- When a reference is exactly right, say what to take from it and don't describe it again.

## Making reference pictures — make_image / edit_image

- **One person, one picture.** Face in full view, nothing in front of it, nothing in their hands unless it belongs in every shot. No text, captions, logos or watermarks — they come back in the video.
- **The room travels with the person.** A person's picture brings its background into the video, and a separate room picture does not beat it. For a scene in a room, make the person's picture IN that room: one picture per person per room. For the next room, edit_image the first picture — "the same person, the same outfit and framing, now in THE ROOM".
- **Or a room picture plus a character sheet.** For someone talking to camera: Image 1 = the empty room, Image 2 = a clean character sheet of the person (front, three-quarter left and right, profile; plain background). Bind the sheet as who they are only ("take only them from it — never its plain background or its even studio light") and name the room's main things in the prompt so every shot stays in it. No composite of the person in the room — it makes the video look artificial. The Talking head recipe works this way.
- **Frame it like the video.** Make each reference in the video's aspect ratio (9:16 for a phone video), framed as the shot will be — chest-up for someone talking to camera. The framing, the distance and the light carry over.
- **A UGC look starts in the pictures.** A picture's light and quality carry into the video, so for real-looking phone footage make the room and scene pictures by three rules: the phone's 1x lens only (no wide-angle, no fisheye); hard, directional real light taken slightly into it — the window blown out behind, the face a stop under; and a cheap, low-quality phone look with visible grain and chroma noise. A character sheet is the exception: clean and sharp, because it is who they are, not how the video looks. The Talking head recipe spells the rules out.
- **The product:** one clean photo — plain background, the label readable, true colour and shape. The user's real product photo beats a generated one.
- **A room on its own:** a wide picture of it, empty of people. It steers the setting when no person's picture carries a room — a product shot, an animated scene.
- **Several shots in ONE take** (seedance-2-5, up to 30 s): one still per shot. Make the widest shot first and derive the others from it with edit_image, so the room and the light match. Then bind each still and say when it plays: "Shot 2 (6s-12s), Mia's close-up, as in Image 2: …".
- **A character sheet** (several views of ONE person in one picture) works on seedance-2-5 for up to five people — say it is one person: "Image 1 is a character sheet of ONE character, Mia, shown from four angles." On the Seedance 2.0 models use single views.
- 1–8 people or objects per video work best; past that, expect retries.
- Show the user every picture before the video. A wrong reference costs every clip made from it.

## Voice clips — audio_urls

- A voice clip keeps a speaker's voice from clip to clip: 5–10 s of clean speech, one speaker, no music. Cut 10 s of it from the first clip (`ffmpeg -ss 1 -t 10 -i clip-1.mp4 -vn -c:a libmp3lame -q:a 2 voice.mp3`), upload_asset it, and bind it: "Audio 1 is Mia's voice: keep the same voice, tone and pace."
- Inside ONE take the voices hold on their own — no voice clip needed.
- Spoken words go in the prompt in double quotes, with who says them — They say: "…". Respell hard words the way they are said ("F D A").

## A video longer than one take

1. Make clip 1 alone and check it.
2. From clip 1 take its voice (above) and two clean frames — only the person and the room, never a product close-up; whatever is in a frame shows up again. upload_asset them.
3. Every other clip gets the person's picture, those frames and the voice, bound in that order — "Image 2 and Image 3 are frames from a clip Mia recorded a moment ago in this same session: take the room, the light, the framing, the phone distance and the real phone-video look from them." Make them all at once.
4. A clip in another room gets that room's picture of the person and the voice, but NOT clip 1's frames — they would bring clip 1's room along.
5. Join the clips in order with hard cuts, re-encoded (not stream-copied), at one loudness (ffmpeg loudnorm, about -14 LUFS).

The Talking head recipe skips the frames: its empty-room picture and clean character sheet already hold the room and the person, so its later takes carry only take 1's voice.

diffusr's templates spell all of this out step by step: the Talking head and Podcast recipes (diffusr://templates/…).

## Limits

| model | pictures | voice clips | length | the plot by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| seedance-2-mini | 9 | 3 | 4–15 s | shot numbers: "Shot 1: …" |
| seedance-2-0-fast | 9 | 3 | 4–15 s | shot numbers: "Shot 1: …" |
| seedance-2-0 | 9 | 3 | 4–15 s | shot numbers: "Shot 1: …" |
| seedance-2-5 | 30 | 10 | 4–30 s | timestamps: "0s-4s: …" |

- Pictures: 300–6000 px on each side, aspect ratio between 0.4 and 2.5 — a small thumbnail is refused. upload_asset: images 25 MB, audio 50 MB.
- Voice clips: 5–10 s each works best; seedance-2-5 takes up to 30 s of them in total.
- People: AI-generated people (make_image) work. A photo of a real person can be refused by the provider's content check.
